summary:
I reviewed the app track (sighurt-browser, sighurt-engine-demo, ci.yml, tools/headless-sway, M3 in STATUS.md) against plan §5, §17, §19–21, §23 M3, §25, §26 and §28, and ran its checks myself. The demo-only build is in good shape.

What I ran:
- `tools/cargo test -p sighurt-browser -p sighurt-engine-demo --no-default-features --features engine-demo`: 17 passed.
- Clippy with `-D warnings` with engine-demo, with engine-demo,engine-wasm and with no engine: clean. `cargo fmt --check`: clean.
- The full end-to-end suite `sighurt-browser/tests/headless.sh` in a private headless sway: 23/23 passed. Output is in scratchpad/review/e2e.
- I looked at main/05, 06, 08, 09, 12, 13 and 14 and config/02. The crosshair in 12 is at output pixel (600, 450), matching the 150 % math.
- The `iterations` counter in the diagnostics confirms the loop sleeps when idle.

The loop, effects, registry, services, persistence, the demo engine and the CI exclusions do what the plan and the report say. I found no unsafe misuse, no page readback copy, no stale-event hole and no unbounded queue.

Problems:
1. `readback_bytes` is a constant 0. Nothing increments it, and `sig` prints it on every frame line. bench/ treats that field as its evidence for the zero-readback criterion, and STATUS cites it too.
2. Page status text outranks `sig`'s own notices. I reproduced this in headless sway: after typing "x" into a page, an invalid configuration was logged as a notice, but the status strip kept showing "Typed into the page: x". The builder changed the demo engine so that `config/00` stops showing the symptom; the ordering itself is unchanged.
3. The Servo renderer line bench/ reads is never printed. Servo starts at launch, so the "first start" branch never runs, and the line has neither `mode=hardware|software` nor `gl=` anyway.
4. `first-frame after_navigate_ms` measures tab-switch time for tabs opened in the background. My run printed 2701 ms and 6313 ms.
5. Several claims are only screenshot-checked or rest on weak tests:
   - motion coalescing never ran in any scenario (`motions_coalesced` stayed 0, and there is no unit test);
   - the buffer-storm check reads the state after 1.5 s of settling, not the peak;
   - the idle check reads `iterations` but never asserts it;
   - address editing, tab switching and coordinates are verified only by screenshots, not by assertions.
6. `sig` with Servo compiled in (its default features) was never compiled. The remote queue on louise-pc is still backed up.

The nits are listed below.
criteria:
Usable address/command editing: VERIFIED. In my run, 06 shows "åäö" in the address line, 07 opens demo://slow and 08 shows "hej åäö" reaching the page; the sighurt-ui tests cover the rest. The end-to-end suite asserts none of this, though: it is screenshot-only.

Reliable tab selection with dummy views: VERIFIED. The diagnostics check (three views, one shown) passed, and screenshots 05, 06, 12 and 13 show the right tab after ctrl-tab, a click and alt-N. The switches after the first are screenshot-only, not asserted.

Bounded buffer lifetime: VERIFIED. The host's unit and protocol tests cover the bound during a storm. The end-to-end check (at most 2 buffers, 0 retiring generations per target) reads only the state 1.5 s after the storm, so it is weak evidence on its own.

No rendering while idle: VERIFIED. In 3 s idle: 1 wakeup (the SIGUSR1 report's own), 0 page frames, 0 chrome paints; `iterations` went 455→456 in a 1 s idle sample. The animation made 124 frames in 2 s with 0 chrome paints, and 0 frames while hidden. The report's "readback_bytes is 0" is a FALSE CLAIM as evidence: it is a constant.

Correct pointer/keyboard coordinates: VERIFIED at 100 % and 150 %. In 06, window (300, 300) is page (300, 216) with the crosshair drawn there. In 12, the buffer pixel is (600.2, 324.3) and the crosshair is on output pixel (600, 450). The scale check (853→1280) passed. 125 % and 200 % were not run end to end (only in the chrome's tests).

Normal close and compositor disconnect handled deliberately: VERIFIED. ctrl-q, SIGTERM and swaymsg kill exit 0 and save the session, which the next start restores. Killing the compositor exits 1 with "the Wayland connection is gone: … Broken pipe" and still saves.

Servo wired behind engine-servo: NOT VERIFIED. It was never compiled; the API names match the current sighurt-engine-servo source only by reading.

Wasm wired behind engine-wasm: VERIFIED to compile (clippy clean). No Wasm page has run in `sig`.

Run on River: NOT VERIFIED. The desktop embargo was in force the whole time.

findings.problem: `readback_bytes` is a hard-coded 0. The counter is never incremented (diagnostics.rs:71-72), and every SIG_DIAG frame line prints a literal `readback_bytes=0` (diagnostics.rs:215). bench/benchlib/parsers.py (SigDiag) says the field is required so that an omitted value can't pass as "no readback", and it turns the counter into the readback metric. For Servo, that metric would read 0 even when `read_to_image` or GL reads happen: Servo counts those itself (`Runtime::readbacks`), but the count only reaches the ignored `engine` line and the JSON. STATUS M3 and the report cite "readback_bytes is 0" as evidence.
findings.fix: Fill in the readback fields from the engines' own counts. On each frame line, report the delta of `runtime.readbacks()` for that engine: as readback bytes (count × the view's buffer bytes), or rename the field to a count and update the parser. Or remove the field until it is measured. Drop the constant-based check from headless.sh and the claim from STATUS.
findings.evidence: diagnostics.rs:71-72 and 215; app.rs has no other write to readback_bytes; bench/benchlib/parsers.py:106 and 143; headless.sh:252-254 checks `d['counters']['readback_bytes']==0`.

findings.problem: The status strip shows the page's status text before `sig`'s own notices (`tab.status.or(error).or(self.notice)`). Any page that sets status text therefore hides configuration errors, refused-permission notices and download results. That goes against §17's trustworthy-UI rule. I reproduced it in headless sway: I typed "x" into demo://pattern and then wrote an invalid config. sig.log has "notice: invalid configuration", but the strip keeps showing "Typed into the page: x" (scratchpad/review/notice/2-invalid-config.png). The builder changed the demo engine so that the test's `config/00` no longer shows the symptom; the ordering was not fixed.
findings.fix: Let browser notices take precedence over page status, at least for a while (for example until the next user action, or a few seconds), or give them their own part of the strip. Add an end-to-end check: set page status, trigger an invalid reload, and assert that the notice is visible.
findings.evidence: app.rs:704-714; decision 46 in STATUS; the builder's open problem 4; my probe script scratchpad/review/notice.sh.

findings.problem: bench/ never gets the Servo renderer line. `diag.renderer` is called only when `open_view` finds the engine `NotStarted` (effects.rs:143, 154-156). Servo is started at launch (`start_at_launch`), so it is already Running and the line is never printed. For the other engines, the line's `mode` is the registry's fixed string ("cpu, wl_shm"), and it has no `gl=` field. bench's SigDiag parser expects `mode=hardware|software gl="..."` (parsers.py:98, 148). The actual GL renderer and the software fallback, which §26 and M1 require, never reach the benchmark harness.
findings.fix: Emit the `renderer` line when an engine's `Runtime::renderer()` first returns `Some`, that is after Servo's first view has a context: `mode=hardware|software gl="<GL_RENDERER>"`. For the CPU engines, print `mode=cpu`.
findings.evidence: effects.rs:142-156; registry.rs:232-243; diagnostics.rs:200-204; my run's sig.log prints `renderer engine=demo mode="cpu, wl_shm"`.

findings.problem: The `first-frame after_navigate_ms` timing is set when a view opens (effects.rs:170) and reported at its first submitted frame. For tabs opened hidden, that is the tab-switch time, not navigation latency. My run printed `after_navigate_ms=2701.467` and `6313.528` for the animation and resize tabs opened at startup. bench/ parses this line as a navigation metric.
findings.fix: Measure only while the view is visible: clear `navigated` on SetVisibility(false), or start the clock only when a navigation begins in a visible view.
findings.evidence: effects.rs:51-56 and 170; app.rs:947-949; scratchpad/review/e2e/main/sig.log first-frame lines.

findings.problem: Several claimed properties are untested or not asserted. (a) Motion coalescing (§19) never ran: `motions_coalesced` stayed 0 in all four scenarios, and the "event coalescing" unit test is the demo engine's, not the loop's. (b) The storm check reads buffers and retiring generations 1.5 s after the storm, not their peak during it. (c) The idle check collects `iterations` but asserts only `wakeups`. A runtime returning `Pending{deadline: None}` spins with timeout 0, and those iterations are not counted as wakeups. (d) Address editing, tab switching by key and click, the 150 % coordinates and the error pages are verified only by screenshots, so a regression would still pass the suite.
findings.fix: (a) Move the motion coalescing in `drain_host_events` into a pure function and unit-test it (same-target runs collapse; a button or key in between keeps order). (b) Record the peak buffer counts, or sample during the storm. (c) Assert that the iterations delta is at most 2 while idle. (d) After each switch, assert through `diag` which view target is `shown`, and check the status text or pixels at known coordinates.
findings.evidence: diag.json from my run: motions_coalesced=0 in main, config, close and disconnect; headless.sh:185-187, 235-242 and 142-171.

findings.problem: The Servo arm (`servo()`, `Runtime::Servo`, `renderer()`/`readbacks()` and `start_at_launch`) has never been compiled; `sig`'s default features build is unverified. The report and STATUS say so, but decision 46 and the ticked criteria read as if the executable were complete.
findings.fix: Run `SIG_WHAT="servo build" tools/remote tools/cargo clippy -p sighurt-browser --all-targets -- -D warnings` before this is committed. Until it passes, mark engine-servo wiring as unverified in STATUS.
findings.evidence: scratchpad/sig/remote-clippy.log ends at 'waiting for another remote run'; the remote queue is still full now (pgrep shows several tools/remote runs pending).

findings.problem: At quit, downloads are cancelled only after the runtimes shut down (app.rs:1099-1107), although §20 says to stop creating work first. The cancel flag is checked only between reads, and the client timeout is 600 s. A stalled server therefore outlives the 500 ms grace and leaves a partial file, despite the module's "no file left behind".
findings.fix: Cancel the downloads first in `shutdown`. Give the client a read timeout (or check the flag with a short timeout), so a cancelled download can remove its file within the grace period.

findings.problem: The Wasm and Servo capabilities are copied by hand (registry.rs:387-391, 414-419) and checked only by a log warning at start. The core decides routing and history from this copy before the runtime exists, so a drift would silently change policy.
findings.fix: Ask the engine crates to export `pub const CAPABILITIES`, as sighurt-engine-demo does, and use them here and in their `capabilities()`.

findings.problem: A view's number for the diagnostics lines comes from trimming its `Debug` string (`format!("{view:?}")` with "ViewId(" removed). If the Debug format changes, bench's `view=` field becomes garbage.
findings.fix: Add an accessor or `Display` to the id newtypes in sighurt-api (an addition only), and use it here.

findings.problem: The resize page's crosshair computes the buffer position with its own ratio (paint.rs:202). The status text uses `Metrics::to_buffer`. The screenshot check of coordinates therefore compares two copies of the formula instead of drawing where the contract's conversion says.

Third-party crates shared with other crates (reqwest, dirs, log, libc, rustls, serde_json, tempfile) are versioned per crate. CLAUDE.md asks for shared versions to be pinned in the root `[workspace.dependencies]`; the comment on reqwest ("so both share one build") relies on keeping two lines in sync.
findings.fix: Move the shared ones to `[workspace.dependencies]` and use `.workspace = true`. This needs the root Cargo.toml lines and the engine crates' owners.

findings.problem: This is the third copy of the keep-it-plugged virtual pointer: experiments/m1-mixed/src/bin/m1-pointer.rs and sighurt-wayland/tests/headless.rs have the other two. The task offered one shared helper in tools/headless-sway.
findings.fix: Keep one helper, for example a small binary built by the headless scripts or an option of tools/headless-sway, and use it from all three.
findings.evidence: grep create_virtual_pointer: the three files above.

findings.problem: A hot-reloaded `[ui.colors] bg` repaints the chrome but not the root window's background: `WindowOptions.background` is set only in `create_window`, and the host has no setter. The fallback shown during a slow resize (screenshot 09) keeps the old color, so the theme applies live only in part.
findings.fix: Ask the host track for a `set_background(window, rgb)`, and call it from `reload_config`.
findings.evidence: app.rs:250-259 and 967-976; sighurt-wayland/src/window.rs:51-62 has no setter.

findings.problem: The module's doc comment doesn't say what it must not own, which CLAUDE.md requires of every module.
findings.fix: Add a "Must not own: …" line, for example browser policy and drawing.

findings.problem: Every notice is logged at info (`log::info!("notice: {message}")`). Notices include page origins from permission prompts and downloaded file names and paths. CLAUDE.md says diagnostics never log page data.
findings.fix: Log only the kind of notice, or lower it to debug without the page-derived parts.
